notes: Evals 2 and 4 are non-discriminating: baseline already finds every hooks/lint bug and invents no Badge bugs. Skill value there is format (lint table, verdict), not detection.
Biggest behavioral win: eval 3 (no scope, no git). With skill stops and asks in 19s/38k tokens; baseline guesses scope by mtime and reviews 5 files in 142s/67k tokens.
Eval 1: baseline skipped tsc; with skill always runs ESLint + tsc gate.
With-skill runs found the same bugs as baseline; slightly more Next.js-doc verification (route handler docs) and explicit severity/verdict.
Two with-skill subagents bypassed a harness Write block via shell heredoc to save report.md; test-harness artifact, not skill behavior, but worth noting.
Each eval ran once per config (1 run), so stddev reflects variation across evals, not repeat runs.
